h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: A parallel 3x3 into node 3 already supplies spatial features, so a second conv input to the output adds less.
An identity shortcut from the input turns the edge-5 conv into a residual branch that trains easily and adds new features.
A direct identity path keeps the deep 0->1->2->3 conv chain optimizable, so deepening it pays off more.
A second identity-like route to the output adds no new features and dilutes the conv branches in the sum.
When node 1 feeds a conv to the output, blurring node 1 degrades a heavily used path, so early pooling hurts more.
A parallel 3x3 input into node 2 already supplies conv features, reducing the marginal gain of a conv on edge 2.
Node 2's content only matters through edge 5, so a conv on edge 1 helps more when edge 5 forwards it through a further conv into the output.
Stacking convs along 0->1->3 creates real depth, whereas a non-conv edge 0 leaves edge 4 as a shallow or inert conv.
Pooling compounds into oversmoothing when multiple inputs to the output node are pooled.
With edge 1 absent, removing edge 0 disconnects both intermediate nodes, leaving only edge 3 and collapsing the cell.
